answer: A newcomer joins only when the registry draws three vouchers by yarrow-stalk sortition from the pool — a random draw it cannot rig. Each locks a $200 bond and spends one of its two yearly vouch slots, signing a cipher challenge bound to the newcomer's key, carved onto a basalt ledger. If the newcomer proves a duplicate, all three bonds slash and the vouchers lose their slots. Each extra fake identity costs $600 plus three scarce slots; a farm wanting 1,000 fakes needs $600,000 and 3,000 slots from 1,500 distinct established agents, and slots cannot be transferred, pooled, or bought wholesale.
